title: Exact sixth-norm noise threshold
statement: Let $\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0\le\rho$. The sixth-norm of $a+\rho b\varepsilon$ is at most the $2$-norm of $a+b\varepsilon$ for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$ and a uniformly chosen sign $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$ if and only if $\rho\le\sqrt{1/5}$.
hypotheses_covered: The norm inequality holds for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$ (left side of the equivalence)
